To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed hierarchical fuzzy-GA approach for the EMS design in microgrids is able to outperform the classic fuzzy-GAs approach, increasing the accounting profits in energy trading, and reducing the RB size, yielding a simpler EMS.
the fuzzy-HGA outperforms the fuzzy-GA approach, increasing the accounting revenue by 67% with a simpler RB, in the energy trading problem considered in this paper.

a hierarchical genetic algorithm (HGA) is applied for tuning the rule base (RB) of fuzzy logic system for flow control in micro grids, and that the HGA rationale focuses in particular on a particular encoding schema, based on control and parametric genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of a novel fuzzy-HGA approach to the synthesis of a fuzzy controller for the management of the energy flows in a microgrid model, showing the potentiality of the proposed methodology in terms of performance and complexity reduction.
the application of bio-inspired techniques in energy trading problems, where a fuzzy-HGA approach is adopted for designing a Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) as an Energy Management System.
the development of a data-driven EMS, which can be easily adapted and tuned to different energy trading problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed fuzzy-HGA scheme, by reducing the number of fuzzy IF-THEN rules, is a more effective and compact solution for the EMS design, allowing to improve the overall accounting profit.

the fuzzy-HGA paradigm, applied to the design of the proposed EMS, is able to improve the accounting profit in the energy trading problem by 67%, while at the same time reducing the number of rules in the RB of the FIS by 40%.
a hierarchical genetic algorithm is a promising technique for tuning fuzzy logic systems in micro grid control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed HGA approach allows to obtain an optimal fuzzy controller for the EMS, reducing at the same time the number of rules in the rule base.

the proposed HGA approach can be considered as a powerful tool for tuning the parameters and for reducing the complexity of the RB of FIS, allowing to achieve better results than the classic fuzzy-GAs.

a hierarchical approach for fuzzy-GA tuning is a good candidate to be used in the design of a fuzzy inference system, in order to obtain a more compact and efficient fuzzy controller, with the advantage of a simpler RB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper hierarchical encoding scheme for the RB of FIS can be exploited for a more efficient tuning of the RB of the FIS, yielding to a simpler and effective fuzzy controller.

, in the considered energy management scenario, a hierarchical genetic approach for the tuning of the RB of a FIS can be successfully exploited in order to improve the performance of the EMS, leading to a more compact and efficient RB.

the proposed fuzzy-HGA approach can be used for the synthesis of EMS in microgrids and other complex systems, where the number of fuzzy-rules can be a priori unknown, while a compact RB is desirable for a better system performance and for a lower computational cost in real-time operation.
